newsitem.title: USA: Russia political changes built into rating - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Russia political changes built into rating - Moody's.

text.p: Russia's political changes are already built into the country's prospective Ba2 sovereign debt rating, and no change in status is anticipated, an analyst at Moody's Investors Service Inc said on Thursday.

"Russia's rating is brand new and was certainly put on to take into account any expectations of more political changes or jockeying," said David Levy, managing director of Moody's sovereign risk unit.
"This is nothing terribly unexpected, and it is already incorporated into the rating."
News on Thursday that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had ousted his security chief Alexander Lebed fueled even more uncertainty in the marketplace over Russia's current political situation.
The news came on the heels of recent heightened concerns over the Russian leader's health.
"The possibility of this type of struggle for influence, not the specific event, was already incorporated into the rating," Levy added.
Moody's issued a prospective Ba2 sovereign ceiling on the foreign currency debt, which will apply to Russia's upcoming Eurobond offering, the analyst said.
